utterances.text: Is there anything the Stanisic Defence wants to respond in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I would ask the Trial Chamber to keep the matter open, and we will conduct investigations to establish what it is the Prosecution say is missing at this time. Obviously -- no, I'll leave it at that. If -- if Your Honours would leave it open, we will do what we can and report back to the Chamber if we cannot do anything more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Of course, we would not like to have it -- I mean, it is apparently a serious challenge to this document, and we are not going to give you forever to -- I want that list. Unless you -- you can indicate what efforts you made and what you did and what the response was and why you need more time, but let's give you -- four weeks from now, would that do?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, four weeks probably wouldn't be sufficient. What we'd ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Six weeks? I mean, what I want to know is you tendered this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- through a witness. The witness says it's all false and -- and then we do not know the person to -- we do not know who wrote the statement, took the statement. Under those circumstances, at a certain moment we have to make up our mind. Either you make a stronger case for admission, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, it was, I'm reminded, served as Rule 68 material. So the difficulty we've got is that it emanates from the Prosecution files. That's the first thing. In order to investigate it and substantiate it, provenance and its reliability, it may take some time. And it may be that this only becomes something we can do during the Defence case. That's why I ask Your Honours to keep the matter open. It's something that we will -- as we look to call evidence to challenge the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I do not know yet whether there will be a Defence case -- well, we'll see whether the -- no, no, because -- let me say the following: If -- if material is disclosed under Rule 68 as exculpatory material, it can all be fabrication lies. I mean, the Prosecution is not there. If someone states for good reasons or for bad reasons that all the accused are innocent and were in Canada at the time when it all happened, then the Prosecution is under a duty to disclose that material because the content of it is -- tends to -- to show the innocence or at least less guilt of the accused. That, of course, doesn't say anything yet about reliability, authenticity of that document. There's a kind of a blind duty for the Prosecutor to -- whatever what looks exculpatory, to immediately disclose that. So I'm not really impressed by that, but we'll consider whether we'll allow you more time, and that is almost indefinite time now --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I can -- I can certainly do -- do more. It was served -- and I can do more within a short period of time because it was served as the transcript from -- or a witness statement from a particular trial in a particular place which has taken place with final adjudication being -- having taken place. So I can provide that level of detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So -- so we'll consider how much time we give you, and you're trying to meanwhile convince us already that you're giving us a serious effort to see whether you can provide us with a little bit more than the document itself, which is challenged as to its authenticity.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We can definitely -- in -- within a week or two provide additional information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll put that -- that's on the record that we might hear from you within two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I earlier made a mistake referring to D -- there seems to be a possible error in the transcript on page 82 where a reference to D85 was transcribed as a reference to D81. Line 17. And I'm always amazed that so little errors of this type exist. We move on. D80 -- no. Let me see. D96. That is a map, a hard-copy map, of Belgrade with the witness's markings on the location of a state security facility. It was marked for identification. There was a problem with the probative value. It was suggested, more or less, to perhaps get better material such as a Google Earth map. It is stuck there. What's your position, Mr. Jordash?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Our position is that the map, whether Google Earth or the map that was originally put to the witness, is not necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You withdraw that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, any problems in withdrawal of the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Then the Prosecution would tender that exhibit, Your Honour. The Prosecution believes it is relevant to the witness's credibility. If the Chamber will recall, it was put to that witness that he had made a mistake about the existence of a state security building there. And if you recall in the evidence of JF-095, I gave him the exact same map. And if the Chamber were to compare the markings of where JF-095 says he met me, it will correspond to where the witness said he met Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, well, of course you could withdraw the document and then have it tendered by Mr. -- under those circumstances, what are we going to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I don't think my learned friend is right about that, but that's for another time, those submissions concerning whether another witness corroborated that map or not. But putting that aside, I think the original problem was that Your Honour felt that the witness's evidence on that map was confused because the witness marked two places, one in error and then another one purportedly in correction of that error. So the last position that Your Honours had taken was that that map did not -- the witness had not testified clearly using that map. But, I mean, if the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if the Prosecution now thinks that there's some -- some -- some value in having it. I mean, then you -- of course, you later would argue that it could be purely coincidence because the witness was confused anyhow. Is that -- well, whatever. But any opposition? Otherwise, we'll --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then any Simatovic problem? D96 is admitted into evidence. And the Chamber will later consider the exact weight to be given to this. Yes. I will not deal with D98 at the moment. The next, which is a series of documents, is D100 plus D101, D102, D105, D106, D110. D100 has one specific issue which distinguishes it from the others, that is, there was a translation issue which is only for this one. Has the translation been verified?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that it was uploaded as 2D161.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but let me see what -- yes. There was an issue about comrade and comrade general. Has now that been a full -- because I noticed that at least -- and, of course, I did not know what the quality of the remainder is, but I noticed that at least one word was not translated. Has the -- has the -- and then we said would you please verify the translation, whether it contains more errors than the one I, with my limited knowledge of the B/C/S, could already identify. Has that been verified?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you give me five minutes, I can then check that with our Case Manager, whether it was checked, whether a corrected version was returned from translation. I can check that right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar informs me that there is one document attached to D100 translation and another translation under the same number not attached. Then I take it that we have to replace the attached document by the newly-uploaded 2D161.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, our Case Manager has just informed me that the translation has been corrected and that it has been checked, and that is the 2D161.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There are two translations with the same number. Could you please specify, then, the document ID number. That would be more clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try to do that. Just give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, you're hereby instructed to link the translation, the corrected translation, and that's the one you received the number of from Mr. Petrovic -- or do you have it already, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can give you the number. So that's 2D01-0842.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's the new translation which now can be linked to D100, and the other one separated from it. Now, there was -- there were other problems with D100, 101, 102, 105, 106, and 110. Let me see. Yes. Whether any extraneous parts of the documents have been redacted from the B/C/S version; that's the first question. Has that been done? I think it was put on your list sent to you last Friday. The second issue is whether the original has been received from Croatian authorities. And the third question was that if so, whether the Simatovic Defence wishes to tender the original document despite outstanding questions in relation to the authenticity. These were the questions we put to you in our ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have been unclear in our instructions to you in the e-mail of last Friday. We'll leave, therefore, this whole series and provide you with clearer instructions next time, but you're invited to have a look at it already. Then I move on to D112. A report of the Office of the Military Prosecutor -- Prosecution, Banja Luka. Here again I think the original -- we're waiting for the original to be tendered, Mr. Petrovic. One of the problems is that these apparently are documents taken, at least it looks like it is, taken from the book "The Homeland War," and then you get the extraneous parts, that is, text which has got nothing to do with the document you wish to tender. And -- so we are seeking clarification. And, of course, we would rather have the original documents rather than an extract of a compilation in the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour. We requested those documents from the Croatian authorities, but we still have had no reply. If the answer does not arrive within the next couple of days, we will ask you for assistance then. And my colleague Mr. Bakrac is reminding me that we need to redact the existing version, that those parts of the document that belong to another document should be removed, because we were reluctant to do that, expecting that the originals would appear so that we don't need to do the same job several times to redact the copy and then the original document. But we cannot -- we can, of course, do this right away if you instruct us to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, we have to -- it's clear that this one will not be resolved. We move on to D118. Translation is missing. Mr. Bakrac, you indicated that it would be an easy thing to do. Has the translation been uploaded?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we do have a translation. This is 65 ter 2D236.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tried to look on e-court just a few minutes ago, and I couldn't see it. I haven't been able to study the document yet, so before the Chamber decides on admissibility, I'd ask for an opportunity to study it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, have you found at translation at least?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Translation is uploaded, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And can be linked to D118. Mr. Groome, could we hear from you by -- let's say by the -- by the end of next week whether there are any objections so that we can decide on admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record. D120 is the same problem, Mr. Petrovic, excerpt from "The Homeland War." Still waiting for the original. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We're waiting for the original. I apologise. Perhaps I missed something. Is this also a translation problem, or is it that there is no original? I don't have 120 as being on my list because there is a translation problem there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can't see immediately whether there is a translation problem. Let me just see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have it on my screen, and there's no translation yet attached to this document in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no translation yet attached. Mr. Petrovic, so apart from getting the original, you're also seeking a --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that there is a translation. It's 65 ter 2D188.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it was not attached to the document then, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Not in e-court. So I'd ask for the same opportunity. And I would point out it -- this does appear to be an original document, not part of the book that we've been referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Petrovic, if you would prepare -- of course, you're still waiting for some responses. But here the issue of original documents of not -- or not, at the time it was tendered, at least according to my notes, it was not the original document, but it was, again, one of the documents found in the -- in "The Homeland War" book. Now if that has been -- if we now have an original document -- Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I stand corrected. I must have put something in wrong. It is the same book that we've --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is the same book. Okay. A translation is there. We're waiting for the original, for you to receive it, and then to tender that original because that's the purpose of this whole exercise. Yes. Earlier you also already indicated that you might seek an order under Rule 54 bis, but that's not -- that was only recently. If you need our assistance, don't hesitate to ask for it. D121.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do have some information about D121 that might resolve the matter rather quickly. D121 was tendered by the Stanisic Defence on the 20th of September. It was a letter from a hospital. I objected to its admission pending an opportunity to do some investigation. I took advantage of having an investigator in the region and asked him to stop by the hospital and speak with the doctor. While it is a matter that still needs further investigation, I believe that based on the conversation with the doctor, the Prosecution should now appropriately withdraw its objection to admission of the letter. I am in possession of a photo of the ledger page. It is being translated. As soon as I have it, I will produce it to both Defence teams for further action, if they deem such as necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But the objection therefore is withdrawn. There was one other issue. You should talk with Mr. -- with the person involved whether we could make this document public. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: He's been spoken to, and there's no objection to it being made public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. D121 is admitted into evidence as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have gone through all the outstanding MFIs. I must reveal to the parties that I have on my agenda quite a number of other matters which range from A to S, mainly minor matters of a technical nature. I do not intend to call a session for that tomorrow. We'll try to see to what extent we can resolve these matters out of court. To the extent it's not possible, they'll be revisited at the next housekeeping session or at any earlier moment which is appropriate. Then we will not sit tomorrow. We adjourn, therefore, until Monday, the 4th of October, at a quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon. And, Madam Registrar, that would be in courtroom ... because Courtroom II is not available yet. In the courtroom to be announced at a later moment. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
